title: Local AI Audit: Map Your Subscriptions to Free Alternatives

sections.title: Audit Your Current AI Spend
sections.prompt: List every AI tool you pay for monthly (APIs, Copilot, cloud notebooks, etc.). For each, write: the dollar cost, the primary task you use it for, and whether that task involves sensitive/proprietary data. Total the annual cost. This is your baseline.

sections.title: Install Ollama and Run Your First Local Inference
sections.prompt: Install Ollama from ollama.com, pull llama3 with `ollama pull llama3`, then run the job-scoring snippet from the blog — substitute a real job description and a summary of your own background. Time the response. Note the latency and whether the JSON output is parseable.

sections.title: Classify Your Tasks: Local vs. Hosted
sections.prompt: Take the tool list from section 1 and tag each task as L (local candidate) or H (hosted). Apply the blog's split rule: batch/async/privacy-sensitive → L; interactive/latency-sensitive/non-sensitive → H. Calculate what percentage of your spend falls in the L bucket.

sections.title: Build a Minimal Overnight Automation
sections.prompt: Design a script (pseudocode is fine if you're not coding yet) that runs on a schedule, sends zero data to external APIs, and produces a ranked or scored output you'd read in the morning. It can be job listings, RSS feeds, a folder of documents — anything real to you. Write the core prompt you'd send to Ollama and the JSON keys you'd want back.

sections.title: Measure the Quality Gap on a Real Task
sections.prompt: Pick one task you currently use a paid API for. Run the same prompt against a local Ollama model (7B or 13B) and against the paid API. Score both outputs on accuracy and usefulness on a 1–10 scale. Write two sentences on where the gap is real and one sentence on whether that gap justifies the cost for this specific task.

cta: Run section 1 right now and drop your annual AI spend total in the comments — then tell us which task surprised you most as a local candidate.
